marian-spencer-statue.description: The Marian A. Spencer statue is Cincinnati's first public statue of a named woman, installed in 2021 in the Women's Garden at Smale Riverfront Park to honor the Cincinnati civil-rights leader and public servant.
marian-spencer-statue.hours: The outdoor statue follows Smale Riverfront Park hours, 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. daily. Visitors 17 and younger must be accompanied by a parent or guardian after 9:00 p.m.; temporary park closures can supersede the schedule.
marian-spencer-statue.location: The statue stands in the Women's Garden in the southeast part of Smale Riverfront Park. The exact pin is Wikidata item Q107694227, corroborated by Cincinnati Parks' public-art and Smale pages.
marian-spencer-statue.parking: Use paid Banks garages or downtown parking, then approach the Women's Garden from Walnut Street or the riverfront promenade. Stadium and riverfront events can change the closest available route.
marian-spencer-statue.restrooms: Cincinnati Parks lists the nearby Walnut Street and Roebling Bridge restrooms from 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. Restroom hours are shorter than park hours and can change with maintenance or river conditions.
marian-spencer-statue.fees: There is no listed admission charge to enter Smale Riverfront Park or view the outdoor statue. Parking, carousel rides, concessions and reserved events are separate.
marian-spencer-statue.accessibility: Smale has paved walkways, elevators and accessible riverfront routes, and Cincinnati Parks says its walkways and features were designed for broad access. Verify elevator status and flood closures before relying on a step-free route.
marian-spencer-statue.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in Smale Riverfront Park. Keep animals controlled in the garden and away from plantings and the sculpture.
marian-spencer-statue.family: The life-size grouping depicts Marian Spencer greeting two children, making it a useful family history stop. Adults should keep children from climbing on the sculpture or planted beds.
marian-spencer-statue.need: This is a memorial and public artwork, not play equipment. Ohio River flooding, major events or maintenance can close parts of the riverfront, so check current Cincinnati Parks notices before leaving.
marian-spencer-statue.imageAlt: Bronze statue of Marian Spencer greeting two children in Smale Riverfront Park's Women's Garden

washington-park-dog-park.description: Washington Park Dog Park is a 12,000-square-foot fenced off-leash area with synthetic canine turf, pea gravel, granite boulders, benches, a play creek and drinking-water spouts for people and dogs.
washington-park-dog-park.hours: The outdoor dog park follows Washington Park hours, 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. daily. Visitors 17 and younger must be accompanied by a parent or guardian after 9:00 p.m.; events, maintenance and posted closures can supersede that schedule.
washington-park-dog-park.location: The fenced dog park is on the east side of Washington Park, next to the Sherwin-Williams Porch. The pin marks the reviewed center of the operator-identified enclosure, not the underground garage entrance.
washington-park-dog-park.parking: The Washington Park Garage is beneath the park, with entrances on Race Street at 13th Street and on Elm Street across from Music Hall. Availability, valet-assist capacity and rates change during events; use an east-side park exit for the shortest dog-park approach.
washington-park-dog-park.restrooms: Washington Park lists public restroom buildings near Elm Street and Race Street. Do not assume indoor access from the garage or Porch outside their posted operating periods.
washington-park-dog-park.fees: The operator lists no admission charge for ordinary use of the dog park. Garage parking, Porch purchases and ticketed or reserved events are separate.
washington-park-dog-park.accessibility: The enclosure uses synthetic turf, pea gravel and paved approaches. Elevators connect the underground garage to park level, but the operator does not describe every part of the creek, boulder or gravel area as wheelchair accessible.
washington-park-dog-park.dogs: Dogs may be off leash only inside the enclosure and must be leashed while entering and exiting. Handlers must remain in view, keep control, carry a leash, remove waste and comply with license, vaccination and aggression rules.
washington-park-dog-park.family: Children under 13 may enter only with an adult. This is an active off-leash enclosure rather than a children's play area; use the separate fenced playground for child-focused recreation.
washington-park-dog-park.need: Entry is at the handler's risk. Remove a dog at the first sign of aggression, keep gates clear, and expect the play creek or water features to be affected by freezing weather or maintenance.
washington-park-dog-park.imageAlt: Fenced Washington Park Dog Park with dogs, boulders, benches and the neighborhood beyond
